known_gaps.description: ResearchWriteOwner.create_research_experiment/cancel_research_experiment have no tenant_id parameter or scoping at all (not just missing enforcement -- the concept does not exist anywhere in this class), and create_research_experiment has no idempotency-key dedup (calling it twice with the same logical request creates two experiments unless the caller explicitly threads the same experiment_id through, which no BFF caller does). cancel_research_experiment also does not touch the parent ticket's lifecycle_history/updated_at the way create_research_experiment does for linked_experiments. The task instructions authorized touching these two files only for such a gap, but adding tenant_id as a new concept to this class (schema change to research.research_experiments' JSON payload, plus tenant-filtering logic mirrored from ResearchWriteOwner's sibling services) is a materially larger change than 'minimal write wiring' and would need an explicit design decision about tenant claim propagation from the BFF identity layer into services/research -- broadening it here risks silently deciding that design question mid-corrective-task. Left both files untouched and record this as an explicit, narrow, follow-up-worthy gap rather than either inventing the fix ad hoc or silently doing nothing without saying so.

These three files (none in the declared 39-path scope list) seed DefaultResearchKnowledgeSourcePort via the now-retired `research_experiments_store=` kwarg and assert on experiment list/get/create/cancel behavior. Since ports/research_knowledge_source.py's in-memory `_experiments` dict is deleted per the accepted decision ('DELETE completely... never falls back to in-memory dictionary'), that kwarg became an inert no-op and these 20 pre-existing tests started failing with 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE. Per this task's own acceptance criteria ('每次搬移同一 accepted head 改完所有現役 consumers 並刪舊 bodies/imports/DI/flags/tests-mocks' -- when migrating an owner, update ALL live consumers, including test mocks, in the same change), these are live consumers of the retired seeding pattern and were repaired in the same commit rather than left broken or deferred to a separate artifact-contract amendment (which additionally could not be requested mid-task since the artifact-contract command is restricted to todo/blocked tasks, not in_progress). Fix applied: each file now defines a small local `_FakeResearchWriteOwner` test double (mirroring services.research.write_owner.ResearchWriteOwner's create/get/list/cancel_research_experiment signatures, including the allowedActions.canCancel projection that the real owner computes) and injects it via the port's `research_write_owner=` constructor kwarg instead of the retired `research_experiments_store=` kwarg. All three files now pass in full: test_rw04_experiment_launch_contract.py (16/18 pass; the remaining 2 failures -- payload['meta']['surfaces']['experiment_status'] returning a dict {'status': 'ok', ...} instead of the bare string this old test expects -- are confirmed pre-existing by reproducing byte-for-byte against the pristine pre-task main.py/experiments.py before this task's own edits, i.e. unrelated meta-shape drift this task did not introduce and is not in scope to fix), test_pathreon_market_persona_fleet_contract.py (full file passes), tests/test_read_surface_port_cutover.py (full file passes).

Per the decision doc's own findings (section 1 evidence table and section 2 per-source detail), none of the five backend services' list/get job endpoints enforce tenant filtering or authentication server-side today (research-worker-gateway, research-orchestrator, training-session, source-ingestion, policy-learning all documented as having 'no tenant parameter or filtering' / 'no FastAPI authentication dependencies' on these specific routes). JobReadPort therefore does not attempt to inject a tenant_id query parameter or bearer token the target services do not support; it forwards no query parameters beyond the native list endpoints' existing contract. Tenant isolation for job reads is enforced at the BFF's own layer (require_read_role / operator identity on GET /bff/jobs*) exactly as before this task, not narrowed or widened by this change. Closing the backend-side tenant/auth gap on each of these five services is out of this task's scope entirely (it is not named as U10A or U10B scope in the decision doc).
